clue.text: Searching for diamonds, found 56 in England

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: the Roman numeral sits inside the abbreviation for England

parts.note: 56 in Roman numerals is LVI (50 + 5 + 1)

explanation.surface: A prospector hunting for gems turns up a find somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is only a link word here; '56' must be read as a Roman numeral, not a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging deeply into something is a figurative way of researching or hunting through it.

clue.text: Perhaps mashed potatoes can be prepared in odd diets

indicators.note: the scrambled can goes inside the letters picked from diets
the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of diets are taken
prepared means the letters of can are made into something new

explanation.surface: Mashed potatoes from a can, perhaps prepared on strange diets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed potatoes' looks like food, but the Mashed Potato was a 1960s dance craze, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mashed Potato is a dance step, so several of them are examples of steps danced.

clue.text: Posh car carries old princess

indicators.note: the car's name holds the princess's name inside

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car make
Di, Diana, the late Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A smart car is carrying a former princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a Lada was a cheap, unglamorous Soviet car, hardly posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentiously refined or affected in manner is a mocking way of saying upper-class.

clue.text: Vehicle's run times troubled conservationists

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of run times are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A vehicle's running times worried the conservation group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' is meant as a means of getting something done, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A means or agent through which something is achieved is a vehicle in the abstract sense.

clue.text: Bird goes savage protecting egg

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround and guard the egg-shaped letter
to savage something is to maul it, so the letters of goes are rearranged

parts.note: O is egg-shaped, a nought

explanation.surface: A bird turns fierce while guarding its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A large waterfowl of the duck family is a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Beginnings of avalanche — rush back in time to shelter

indicators.note: the picked letters plus the abbreviation go inside the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words avalanche and rush are taken

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for back, as in football positions

explanation.surface: As an avalanche starts, climbers dash back to find cover in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush back' looks like one instruction, but 'rush' only gives its first letter and 'back' is B.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven or port gives ships protection, and as a verb it means to give refuge to.

clue.text: Strike gold! 1,001 dollars at random

parts.note: to hit is to strike
or is the heraldic word for gold
M is 1,000 and I is 1 in Roman numerals
the dollar sign looks like S, so two of them stand for dollars

explanation.surface: Someone strikes it rich, winning a thousand-and-one dollars by sheer chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Done haphazardly, with no plan, so success is down to luck.

clue.text: God at home with warmer 21?

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A god stays home beside a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 Across is SNOW; the warmer version of that precipitation is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When the air is above freezing, falling water arrives as drops rather than flakes.

clue.text: One sees no upset ladies next to king and queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word no upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a loo is a lavatory, such as the ladies'
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone notices an annoyed set of ladies beside a royal couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander or spectator is someone who watches events without joining in.

clue.text: Ringtones are annoying

indicators.note: annoying means disturbing, so the letters of tones are are stirred up

explanation.surface: A grumble that mobile phone ringtones are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is hidden in the front of 'Ringtones': the rest of that word joins 'are' as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo or reverberate with sound is to ring out.

clue.text: Students' union is full of extremely decorative posers

indicators.note: the union's abbreviation holds the picked letters inside it

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' union

indicators.note: the outermost letters, first and last, of decorative are taken

explanation.surface: The students' union is packed with showy people striking attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Life models who pose unclothed for art classes are sitters, here called posers.

clue.text: Unconscious, if sled crashes in playing areas

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out

indicators.note: a sled that crashes is wrecked, so its letters plus if are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked out when a toboggan crashes on the pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball the far parts of the field are where fielders play away from the batter.

clue.text: Chuck senior's fruit?

parts.note: an elder is someone senior in age or rank
Chuck Berry was the American rock and roll guitarist

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether some older man named Chuck has fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a verb meaning throw, but it is the rocker Chuck Berry; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The small dark berries of the elder tree are used in wine and cordials.

clue.text: Satellite's second leg

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A spacecraft's second stage, or leg of a journey, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' is the cricket on side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth's natural satellite orbits the planet; any planet's natural satellite is called this too.

clue.text: One small drink during meeting? 500 get wasted

indicators.note: the pieces fall within the word for a meeting

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a sip is a small drink
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: One small drink on a date leads to five hundred getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' suggests drunk, but here it means squandered or frittered away.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or energy squandered on pleasure has been frittered away.

clue.text: Wonderful film 7?

definitions.meaning: the 1960 western The ... Seven, with the word before the number

explanation.surface: A rave review of a film, with a nod to a number.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is the number in the film's title, not a cross-reference to 7 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid or superb things earn this word of high praise, and it names a famous western with seven gunmen.

clue.text: Sensitive reactions as government moves to the front balconies

indicators.note: the letter for government is shifted to the start of the word

parts.note: allergies are the body's sensitive reactions to substances

explanation.surface: Political allergies arise as the government comes forward to the balconies.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper floors projecting over a theatre's main hall are its upper tiers of seating.

clue.text: Worst all over — upper-class girl kidnapped by parliamentarian

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is turned over and read the other way
the class letter and girl are held inside the parliamentarian

parts.note: MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
U denotes upper-class usage
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl kidnapped by an MP: the worst possible scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' means the whole thing is turned around; it is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, the least favourable conditions for an organism are its worst, the opposite of the optimum.

clue.text: Went with piece of furniture containing English pine

indicators.note: the furniture holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture
to pine for is to long for

explanation.surface: Someone went off with a bed made of English pine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the wood, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go together are associated, as a lid fits with a jar.

clue.text: Makes immortal and gives reality to losing vote

indicators.note: the cross that marks a vote is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: to externalise a thought is to give it outward, real form
X is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Someone immortalises things and makes them real, though losing an election.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something last for ever is to make it everlasting, so immortalising fits.

clue.text: Introductions to masters in relativity: time's an illusion

indicators.note: the first letters of masters, in and relativity are taken

parts.note: an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Einstein's lesson for masters students: time itself is an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical effect in hot deserts makes distant water appear where none exists.

clue.text: Against suppressing language of poetry

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits on top of and holds down the language

parts.note: VS, versus, means against
Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: Opposition to suppressing the language of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of metrical writing make up poems, so lines of poetry.

clue.text: It falls slowly to begin with, at present

indicators.note: only the opening letter of slowly is used

parts.note: now means at the present time

explanation.surface: Something drifts down slowly at first and is falling right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of frozen precipitation drift down from winter clouds, so it is something that falls.

clue.text: I crept about, caught by quiet woman being alert

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are held inside the quiet letter and the woman's name

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Eve, the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: about signals the letters of I crept being moved around

explanation.surface: Someone crept around but was spotted by a silent woman keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp and quick to notice things is observant, keenly aware.

clue.text: Animal caught by doctor (male)

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of male are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal captured by a vet, noted as being male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a vet treating the animal, but it is the verb meaning alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A humped desert beast of burden is a large mammal.

clue.text: Plain wholesome ready-made sandwiches

indicators.note: the words hold the run of letters between them like a sandwich filling

explanation.surface: Simple, healthy, pre-packed sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food, but it is the verb: the words enclose the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is nothing more than it seems is simple or bare, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Element of seaming movement with Underwood's first maiden

indicators.note: movement of the letters of seaming means they are rearranged
only the initial letter of Underwood is taken

parts.note: M marks a maiden over, one with no runs, in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Seam bowling movement from Derek Underwood, the England spinner, yields a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaming and maidens point to cricket; Derek Underwood was an England bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A light silvery metal with atomic number 12 is a chemical element.

clue.text: They might be shed by tense organs

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ears are organs of hearing

explanation.surface: Tense organs that might shed something, like an anxious body.
explanation.definitionFit: Drops of salt water are wept from the eyes, so they are something shed when crying.

clue.text: Group from the '80s and Blur in trouble

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to be in a mess is to be in trouble

indicators.note: to blur is to smudge, so the letters of and are muddled

explanation.surface: Two British bands, an '80s ska group and the 90s Britpop outfit Blur, get into a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blur' looks like the Britpop band, but it is the anagram signal; the answer is the Nutty Boys ska band.
explanation.definitionFit: The London ska-pop band behind Our House had many hits in the 1980s.

clue.text: 50+ queens have problems in hosiery

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
the plus sign means add
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen; two of them make ERS

explanation.surface: Fifty-plus queens have trouble with their stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs in tights or stockings, where a line of stitches unravels, are called by this name in Britain.
